text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: redis-primary-1 maxclients reached (service: redis-prod, env: us-east-1). Page to oncall: kira. Metric spike: redis_connected_clients 100000 -> 100500 in 2m.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident fired (#PD-9842). Acknowledge required by kira.

kira: acked. I'll take it. on my way to runbook.

mira_prod: seeing 502/504s from api-prod-high; trace sample: requests hang on redis GET for >2s then timeout. Error rate up ~1.8% on checkout flow.

alex_backend: logs from app-pod-17 show: "(err=IOError) connect to 10.2.5.12:6379: connection refused" then retry storm. Also a bunch of `read: connection reset by peer`.

tony_db: looking at redis metrics: `maxclients` threshold hit, `connected_clients` pegged. Memory/CPU fine. Network TX errors on redis-primary-1 nic increasing (ifconfig shows TX dropped packets). Suspect ephemeral connection storm from new rollout or client pool leak.

kira: immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle traffic from gateway to reduce client churn 2) try to increase redis `maxclients` at runtime 3) spin up a warm standby redis and shift some non-critical traffic.

jordan_sre: agree. I can flip a feature-flag to shed non-essential reads (analytics, experimental endpoints) to reduce client count. alex, can you identify the biggest offending route?

alex_backend: looks like /v1/embeddings/batch and /v1/session/state causing most connections. I'll push guardrails to batching layer to limit concurrent connections per worker.

mira_prod: setting temporary rate-limit on checkout route to 20r/s in edge to keep customers mostly unaffected but cut noisy background traffic. Pushing now.

ops-bot: Executed: feature-flag toggle `ff/redis-safe-shed` -> true (user: mira_prod).

kira: attempting runtime increase of maxclients on redis-primary-1. Command: `redis-cli -h redis-primary-1 CONFIG SET maxclients 200000`

tony_db: running that now. If NIC is dropping packets we might still see failures, but worth trying while we scale.

ops-bot: Command output (redis-primary-1):
```
OK
```

tony_db: CONFIG SET succeeded. connected_clients immediately dropped ~40k after shed flags and rate-limit. We still see ~60k clients but stable. TX drops decreased.

jordan_sre: spinning a new redis-primary-2 (warm replica promoted for non-critical keys). Provisioning via infra autoscale: `terrform apply -var 'env=prod' -target=module.redis_cluster.add_node`. ETA ~4m.

alex_backend: deployed connection-pool backpressure change to batching worker: max_conns_per_worker=10. That should stop the storm.

mira_prod: edge rate-limit in effect, errors on checkout dropping back to baseline. Observability: 95th latency for checkout down from 2.5s to 600ms. Customer errors trending down.

kira: good. commands and notes:
- `CONFIG SET maxclients 200000` applied
- `ff/redis-safe-shed` enabled to shed non-critical routes
- edge rate-limit applied to checkout at 20r/s
- started add-node for redis cluster

ops-bot: redis-primary-2 node created and joined cluster. Promotion step pending.

tony_db: promoted new node as secondary and started migrating some clients via proxy config. We're moving analytics/embedding keys over first.

jordan_sre: swapped proxy routing for non-critical traffic to redis-primary-2. Commands used: 
```bash
kubectl patch svc redis-proxy -n infra -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"role":"redis-primary-2"}}}'
```

mira_prod: traffic on main cluster normalized. Error rate back to ~0.2%. API latency recovered. Customer-facing impact minimal after mitigations.

alex_backend: leaving a short-term mitigation PR to limit batches and add circuit-breaker. We'll ship proper pooling fix next sprint.

kira: marking incident as stabilized. PagerDuty: add note and resolve when oncall hands off.

pagerduty: Incident #PD-9842 acknowledged by kira at 3312345682. Status: acknowledged.

ops-bot: Automated playbook link: https://playbooks.redwood.ai/redis/conn-surge (ref: runbook-redis-conn-surge).

jordan_sre: taking handoff for follow-up/RCAs. I'll run full postmortem and coordinate with infra to tune connection pooling. Kira — any notes for the doc?

kira: notes for RCA: probable cause: sudden client connection increase from new batch workers + lack of connection pooling + NIC TX drops on primary -> maxclients hit. Temporary fixes: runtime maxclients increase, shed traffic, repoint non-critical to new node. Long term: connection pooling, batch guardrails, improved autoscaling for redis node NIC->cpu thresholds.

mira_prod: customer impact summary: small percentage (~1.8% peak) of checkout requests experienced timeouts for ~8 minutes. No major data loss. ops to notify accounts for any anomalies.

jordan_sre: noted. I'll open postmortem ticket and assign owners. Kira handing back to me at 3312346234.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: PagerDuty: incident resolved (PD-9842) by kira -> handed to jordan_sre for RCA.

kira: thanks team. I'll be available for any follow-ups. :thumbsup:

alex_backend: will follow up with PR and tests.

tony_db: will schedule infra change to monitor NIC drops as a threshold for autoscale.

jordan_sre: closing thread, will postpostmortem in #postmortems once ready.

ops-bot: Thread archived to incident-log.
